Let’s dig into Chapter 8: Nurturing the Element in Ourselves.
You know, finding your Element isn’t something you just stumble upon once and you’re done. It’s really a journey—one where you listen to yourself, try new things, and notice what actually gives you energy and joy. For a lot of us, the toughest part is simply letting ourselves explore. The world is always telling us what’s practical, what’s responsible, what’s “normal.” But stepping outside those lines? That takes real courage.
There’s a story I love—a man who spent years working in IT. Deep down, though, he always felt this pull to the outdoors. Hiking, birdwatching, learning about local ecosystems—they lit him up. But for ages, he brushed those passions off as just hobbies, not “real” work. Then, after a health scare, he decided to volunteer with a conservation group. Suddenly, his world opened up. He started taking courses in environmental science, and before long, he found a job that let him blend his tech skills with his love of nature.
Most people miss the small clues pointing toward their Element. It might be an activity that makes time fly, a topic that sparks your curiosity, or even something that just comes naturally to you. Sometimes, it’s when others turn to you for help in a certain area. Paying close attention to these little signals—that’s often the very first step toward something new.
Trying new things is huge here. Even experimenting in small ways can uncover hidden talents or unexpected interests. Take the woman who loved baking. She started sharing her treats with neighbors, and their encouragement nudged her to start a small business. In the process, she found a sense of purpose that her old office job never gave her.
It’s so easy to get stuck in routines, to think that change is too risky or that it’s just too late. But the stories of people who find their Element? They’re packed with second chances and surprising twists. Being willing to start as a beginner, to mess up, and to learn as you go—that’s what really makes the difference.
Support matters, too. Sharing your dreams with trusted friends, finding mentors, or joining groups with similar interests can give you that boost and keep you accountable. The journey honestly feels lighter when you’re not walking it alone.
Most importantly, nurturing the Element is about honoring what feels true to you. Even carving out just a few minutes a day for what brings you joy can start to reshape your life. Over time, those small moments add up, and you’ll find yourself living in a way that feels more authentic—and a whole lot more fulfilling.
